industry.key: P. Energy, commodities and metals mining
industry.why: Overweight, carried. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: B now, A prior at the industry, with Downstream distribution A, Upstream A, Services D and Metals and mining F inside it. No Brent level reached the pack, so the condition (Brent under $85) is untested, and the undated headline that oil is dipping on peace hopes is noted, not acted on. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only): energy is still the hedge inside a European book against the shock that hurts everything else, and the hedge has not been needed for two weeks. Eight of the top 40 on the starting score are energy names, from 15 last week, as Neste and Galp left the Pool. Counter-case: the tilt scorecard's negative spreads are consistent with the Overweight having been paid already, and a ceasefire would take the premium out. To C if Brent is read under $85 or the industry's relative strength falls to C.

sector.why: Double Overweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): Brent $111 (Jefferies, 22 Oct), oil above $100 and rising, energy led the week, and refining and distribution are the beneficiaries of disruption whatever the oil price does next; the refining margin benchmark was not re-read this week, so the condition written on the row (back to B if the margin falls below $40 a barrel or Brent below $85) is tested on Brent alone and has not fired. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: A now, A prior. Seven Pool names; Neste is first on the starting score. Counter-case: Goldman attributes part of the oil move to restocking, and two months into leadership is where reversals begin.

geography.why: Double Underweight, carried on a stale reading, said plainly: the French premium (a record 150 basis points on 26 October) was not re-read, no source spoke to France, and the conditions (to D under 120 basis points for a month; to C under 100) could not be tested. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). TotalEnergies is 36th on the starting score with a global revenue base the row does not describe well. Counter-case: Moody's affirmation and the contrarian set-up in French small and mid caps. A week without a spread reading is not a reason to lift a row set on one; re-test when the premium is read.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
